date_note: Kukmin Ilbo (23 November) says the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education learned of the leak on 20 November, the survey's last day, and sent a text notice to users on 23 November; the exposure ran during the survey from 3 November.
exec: A public library survey page exposed names and phone numbers of participants; how the data was viewed is still under investigation.
geo_basis: victim: Jeongdok Library in Jongno-gu, Seoul, as the article states
org: Jeongdok Library (Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education)
plain: Names and mobile numbers of 636 people who took a Seoul public library's website survey leaked from the page that collected details for gift vouchers; officials are investigating whether it was hacking.
summary: Names and mobile numbers of 636 people (936 counting duplicates) who took Jeongdok Library's website satisfaction survey leaked from the survey's gift-voucher page, Kukmin Ilbo reports. An education office official said the data was viewed by abnormally manipulating the homepage's screen code and that whether it was an outside intrusion or an insider is under investigation. The office reported it to the Ministry of Education and the Personal Information Protection Commission.
title: Seoul's Jeongdok Library survey page leaks names and phone numbers of 636 people

validation.note: Kukmin Ilbo exclusive read in full; it quotes the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education's text notice and an official. No second publisher or official notice found by search.
